transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20251029-edgewise-01
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Adrian Torres (Edgewise Head of ML), Priya Rao (CTO), Luke Harris (SRE), Nadia El-Khoury (PM)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
Edgewise is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for clinical summarization and search. Primary concerns: context length for long patient records, multilingual support (Spanish + Arabic), tool-calling to query EHRs, HIPAA/SOC2, VPC/networking, and predictable latency for triage flows. They asked about open-model tradeoffs (Falcon, Mistral, Llama families), quantization, and KV cache effects. Next steps: run benchmarks and share security docs + pricing.

Topics:
- context length & KV cache
- model family comparisons (accuracy vs cost)
- tool calling and function / streaming support
- deployment mode tradeoffs (hosted/dedicated/private)
- security/compliance (SOC2/HIPAA, KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Samir our SE. How are you all?
[00:04] Adrian Torres: Good, thanks. Quick intro: I'm Adrian, Head of ML. We run clinical summarization and an internal triage assistant. We're trying to decide whether to keep hosted for speed or go Dedicated/Private for compliance and latency predictability.
[00:11] Maya Chen: Great, that's what we want to sort through. Samir, want to frame tradeoffs?
[00:13] Samir Patel: Sure. Big levers are model selection (open vs commercial), context length and caching, and infra mode — hosted is fastest to ship, Dedicated gives predictable throughput, Private gives full network control and air-gap options. For your use case — long patient records and tool calling to fetch EHR rows — we usually look at long-context variants and KV/prefix caching.
[00:29] Priya Rao: When you say long-context, what numbers are we talking? Our longest notes are like 40k tokens.
[00:33] Samir Patel: Right. Models vary. We have verified configs for ~32k contexts on some Llama- and Mistral-derived variants. There are experimental routes for 128k+ but that changes latency and memory characteristics—often needs model sharding or specialized kernels. For 40k tokens, we'd recommend a 64k-capable model or streaming + smart KV cache to avoid re-encoding entire history for each call.
[00:49] Luke Harris: Is KV cache the same as prefix cache? We have many repeated sections across notes.
[00:51] Samir Patel: Similar idea. We cache key-value pairs for the transformer so repeated prefixes don't re-cost tokens. Redwood's runtime can do auto-prefix caching per customer/model route; it helps a lot for repeated clinical templates. But cache hit rates depend on prompt engineering.
[01:05] Adrian Torres: Okay. And on open model accuracy—we've been comparing Falcon and Mistral and also looking at Llama 2/3 forks. Cost-wise Falcon seemed cheaper, but performance for clinical extraction was worse in our initial eval. Thoughts?
[01:16] Samir Patel: That's common. Falcon and Mistral trade parameterization and pretraining differences. Mistral-7B variants often punch above weight for instruction tasks, but larger Falcon or Llama families can give better factuality after fine-tuning. Important to run evals on a held-out clinical set — Redwood can help run those benchmark runs on Hosted or Dedicated and give token-level cost breakdowns.
[01:35] Priya Rao: Can you support fine-tuning or are we limited to parameter-efficient methods? HIPAA prevents us from sending raw patient data to hosted endpoints unless we have Business Associate Agreement in place.
[01:44] Maya Chen: We have a HIPAA-ready process for enterprise customers including BAA options on Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we do offer controlled ingest under certain enterprise agreements; many customers choose Dedicated or Private to avoid regulatory lift. Regarding tuning: we support fine-tuning on Dedicated or Private but often recommend instruction-tuning or adapters to limit data exposure.
[02:02] Nadia El-Khoury: Multilingual — we'll need Spanish and Arabic support. How mature are open models there?
[02:06] Samir Patel: Some models handle Spanish well; Arabic is trickier. We see variance: Llama-derived and certain Mistral variants handle Spanish robustly, but Arabic requires targeted evals — tokenization can blow up token counts. We recommend subword-aware tokenization checks, and again benchmark with your prompts. Redwood's Optimize tool can simulate tokenization and estimate cost across languages.
[02:28] Adrian Torres: On tool-calling, we need the model to call an internal EHR query tool to pull labs. How does Redwood support function or tool calling?
[02:34] Samir Patel: We support several patterns: synchronous function-calling (model returns a structured payload), an outbound tool-hook to your service, and streaming tool results back into the model. For sensitive data we usually run tool execution inside customer VPC or via a secure webhook over mTLS. You can pin the tool-call route to Dedicated capacity so latency is bounded.
[02:51] Luke Harris: If the model calls our webhook, what about retries and backpressure? We need idempotency and controlled rate limits.
[02:57] Samir Patel: Good point. Redwood supports configurable retries, rate limiting per route, and request queuing. For high-sensitivity flows we recommend Dedicated with a private network path and SAML SSO for role-based access to keys.
[03:09] Priya Rao: Encryption—KMS/HSM options? We need customer-managed keys.
[03:12] Maya Chen: Yes. Private and Dedicated support CMK via KMS and integrations with your HSM provider in Private deployments. We also maintain audit logs and token-level usage traces that can be streamed to your SIEM.
[03:24] Adrian Torres: Can you share SOC2 artifact or a summary right now?
[03:26] Maya Chen: We'll send the SOC2 summary and HIPAA annex following this call. Samir, we'll attach the security whitepaper.
[03:31] Samir Patel: I'll add links in the follow-up.
[03:33] Adrian Torres: Great. Cost — we need 95th percentile latency under 400ms for triage paths; otherwise clinicians complain. Is that realistic on Dedicated with larger models?
[03:44] Samir Patel: Depends on model and quantization. With int8 or int4 quantized variants and GPU-backed Dedicated pools, we've seen sub-200ms for 2k-4k token responses on optimized kernels. For 32k contexts, latency increases — often in the 500ms-2s range depending on generation length. But you can route critical low-latency flows to smaller context models and use incremental retrieval from KV caches to keep latency low.
[04:08] Nadia El-Khoury: So architecture-wise, we could do hybrid: Hosted for day-to-day non-PHI, Dedicated for PHI triage, Private for legal/regulatory zones?
[04:15] Maya Chen: Exactly. Many customers use a hybrid routing policy: low-cost hosted for asynchronous tasks, Dedicated pinned for clinical real-time flows, and Private for on-prem or air-gapped requirements. Redwood routing can failover automatically if capacity is constrained.
[04:27] Priya Rao: About model updates—how do rollouts work? We can't have silent model changes in triage flows.
[04:32] Samir Patel: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and pinning model versions per route. You can enforce approval gates and automatic rollback if quality metrics degrade. We also integrate with prompt-based evals so you can track regressions.
[04:45] Adrian Torres: Great. Any gotchas around tokenization? We saw token count differences across models blow our budgets.
[04:49] Samir Patel: Yes, tokenization variance is real. For example, languages like Arabic can be higher token density. Redwood Optimize runs tokenization simulations across model family to estimate costs per 1k prompts. We'll include that report in the follow-up.
[05:00] Luke Harris: For the pilot, what would you recommend we start with?
[05:03] Maya Chen: I'd propose a two-week Dedicated pilot: run your prompt set against Mistral- or Llama-derived 64k-capable variants with KV caching enabled, plus a smaller 4k model for low-latency triage. SE-led benchmark: latency, token cost, and QA metrics. Samir to scope.
[05:15] Samir Patel: Yep, I'll draft the benchmark plan: dataset, metrics, and infra. We'll run both Hosted and Dedicated runs so you see delta.
[05:21] Nad ia El-Khoury: (overlap) Sorry, quick—what about streaming outputs for clinician UI?
[05:24] Samir Patel: Supported. We stream partial tokens and can include tool-call triggers mid-stream. There's some complexity with function-calling mid-stream but we've implemented it for a few customers.
[05:34] Priya Rao: Would we need Private to get audited access logs for compliance?
[05:38] Maya Chen: Dedicated includes audit logs and long-term retention as an add-on. Private gives the most control if you need internal auditors to access raw logs on-prem.
[05:46] Adrian Torres: Any competitor feature gaps we should be aware of?
[05:49] Maya Chen: Many competitors have strong APIs but fewer baked-in production features like prefix KV caching, automatic batching tuned for latency SLOs, and unified routing across hosted/dedicated/private. But Anthropic and OpenAI have large model families and managed fine-tuning. We'll include a comparison table in follow-up.
[06:03] Luke Harris: Can you reprovision Dedicated capacity quickly? Our load could spike during audit windows.
[06:06] Samir Patel: Dedicated pools can autoscale with burst capacity options. There are commit tiers—burst can be used for short windows. We'll show quota/burst costs in the pricing doc.
[06:14] Maya Chen: Quick recap then: Redwood to send pricing, security docs, pilot SOW, and Samir to scope benchmarks. Edgewise to share prompt corpus and success metrics.
[06:23] Adrian Torres: Sounds good.
[06:25] Maya Chen: Anything else?
[06:27] Priya Rao: No, that's all for now. Thanks.
[06:29] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday with docs and a proposed pilot schedule.

End of transcript.
